question: What is the main job of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit (TSSU)?

options.A: Disposing of hazardous biological waste from wards
options.C: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing medical instruments

explanation: You've got this! The TSSU is the heartbeat behind every clean surgery. Its main job is to safely clean, sterilize, and hand out surgical tools so patients stay infection-free. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do hospitals prefer a centralized TSSU instead of letting individual wards clean their own surgical tools?

options.A: It reduces the cost of purchasing brand new instruments
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for chemical disinfectants
options.C: It allows nurses to spend more time at the patient bedside
options.D: It ensures consistent and strict quality control standards

explanation: Great thinking! When trained specialists handle sterilization in one central place, you can trust that every single instrument goes through the exact same high safety checks every time. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which area in the TSSU uses negative air pressure?
explanation: Spot on! The dirty (decontamination) zone has negative air pressure so that air flows inward, trapping germs and stopping them from floating out into cleaner rooms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why must work inside the TSSU always flow in one direction?

options.A: To reduce the electricity consumption of heavy sterilizing machines
options.B: To prevent clean and sterile items from mixing with dirty ones
options.C: To make it easier for nursing students to clean the floors
options.D: To speed up the physical movement of heavy instrument trays

explanation: Exactly! Keeping a one-way workflow ensures items only move forward from dirty to clean, protecting patients from cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: When first rinsing used surgical instruments, why should you use cool water instead of hot water?

options.A: Hot water causes proteins to bake onto the metal surface
options.B: Cool water makes the instruments easier to grip with gloves
options.C: Cool water is cheaper for hospital utility budgets
options.D: Hot water damages the outer coating of stainless steel

explanation: You're learning fast! Heat actually cooks blood and proteins, making them stick like glue to the metal. Always start with cool water to rinse them right! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: A nurse notices dried blood on a clamp coming out of the washer. What should be done?

options.A: The cleaning process was incomplete and the instrument must be re-washed
options.B: The instrument is permanently stained but still safe to use
options.C: The autoclave cycle reached too high a temperature
options.D: The packaging material was sealed incorrectly

explanation: Spot on! If you still see dirt or blood, the washing stage failed. Any leftover organic matter blocks sterilization, so back to the wash it goes! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: What should you do with a surgical instrument that has a broken ratchet during inspection?

options.B: Stored in the sterile room for minor procedures
options.C: Sent straight to the sterilization autoclave
options.D: Wrapped tightly in a double linen layer

explanation: You got it! Damaged tools won't work right during surgery and tiny cracks can hide bacteria. Pull them out of use right away. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why must the packaging used for steam sterilization be porous (able to let air and steam through)?

options.A: To ensure the wrapper dissolves completely inside the machine
options.B: To make the heavy trays lighter for nurses to carry
options.C: To let air escape so the package smells fresh when opened
options.D: To allow the sterilizing agent to penetrate and reach the instruments

explanation: Brilliant! Steam needs to touch every single surface of the tools inside to actually kill the germs. Porous wraps let the steam in safely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the most trusted and widely used method of sterilization in the TSSU?

options.A: Boiling in water for ten minutes
options.D: Steam under pressure in an autoclave

explanation: You're doing great! The autoclave is the gold standard because hot steam under pressure quickly destroys all germs and tough spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: What do biological indicators test for when placed inside a sterilizer?

options.A: The total weight of the metal trays loaded into the chamber
options.B: The correct color change of paper tape on instrument packs
options.C: The actual destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores
options.D: The exact temperature of the room surrounding the machine

explanation: Spot on! Biological indicators use real, super-tough live spores to prove that the machine is strong enough to kill the hardest-to-beat germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: In the TSSU, what does the inventory rule 'FIFO' stand for?
explanation: Correct! FIFO means the supplies that arrived first get used first, keeping items from sitting on shelves past their expiration dates. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse drops a sterile instrument pack on the theatre floor before opening it. What is the correct next step?

options.A: Place the pack back on the shelf for the next procedure
options.B: Open the pack and check if the metal inside looks clean
options.C: Return the pack to the TSSU for complete reprocessing
options.D: Wipe the outside wrapper with alcohol and use it anyway

explanation: You've got this! Once a sterile pack hits the floor, its protective barrier is compromised. You can't trust it anymore—send it back for complete re-sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT safe for staff working in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Putting on face shields and eye protection

explanation: Great catch! Open-toed shoes leave your feet exposed to falling sharps and dirty splashes. Always wear closed, protective shoes in the wash area! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) so important specifically in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Hospital management requires it only for decorative uniformity
options.B: It prevents dust from settling on the clean instruments
options.C: The temperature in that specific room is extremely high
options.D: Staff are exposed to blood splashes, contaminated water, and sharp tools

explanation: Spot on! Because you are washing blood-stained, used instruments, PPE acts as your shield against splashes, dirty water, and accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)
